s.intro: Here the program collects what does not convince it and learns by itself. Each check counts favourable (+) and contrary (−) outcomes per kind and callsign: after 3 matching outcomes an automatic rule is born, valid until an opposite outcome calls it into question. Your decisions (Good, Drop) always win; ↺ hands the decision back to the program. Rules are kept in Dati/APPRENDIMENTO.TXT next to the program.
s.d.eme: Q65 or JT65 over 1000 km with the Moon above the horizon at both ends, or EME in the comment: excluded like meteor scatter. Stations that often fall here are learned as EME stations. Good = their long paths are treated as tropo.
s.d.lungo: Over 1000 km, held in quarantine until confirmed. Revealed = +, expired unconfirmed = −. Good = that station's long paths show at once; Drop = never.
s.d.ascolto: PSKReporter receiver discarded because the stations it reports are on other bands (−), or rehabilitated by human DX clusters (+). Good = never discarded; Drop = always.
s.d.locatore: The received square is not the one in CALL3.TXT. If the station keeps sending it, the program learns it has moved and uses the received square. Drop = CALL3.TXT always wins.
s.d.centro: 6-character locator ending in LL or MM: many automatic sources truncate the locator and pad it with the square centre. CALL3.TXT is used when it has the same square. Information only.
s.d.skimmer: Callsign with -SDR, /SDR, -# or -n (RBN skimmers, PSKReporter receivers): the locator is looked up with the base callsign. Information only.

c.title: Changes to CALL3.TXT
c.help: CALL3.TXT is never touched: changes live in two layers on top of it. Entries typed here win over everything, even the locator the station sends. Added files (same CALL,LOCATOR format) win over CALL3.TXT; with several files the last in alphabetical order wins. Callsigns with a slash (IV3/HB9CAT, F/IC8TEM) are written as they are.
s.d.cluster: In DM4X and RBN automatic spots the first locator (e.g. KN09tp<>KN09) is the one the spotting station declares for itself. If it has 6 characters and the database says otherwise, the program corrects it in Dati/CALL3-CLUSTER.TXT. Manual entries always win. Information only.

c.g7_help: Only for callsigns without a 6-character locator in any other source; only 6-character locators not centred (LL/MM) are accepted. Data collected automatically by api.g7vrd.co.uk, a hobby service: at most 40 lookups per minute, each callsign once a day. Results in Dati/CALL3-G7VRD.TXT.

u.disc_p1: LIVETROPOVHF makes a semi-probabilistic calculation of tropospheric propagation at VHF and UHF. It uses the vertical profiles of the GFS weather model (NOAA) and the theory of the scientific papers listed in the «Sources and formulas» manual: the indices come from the physics of ducts, while thresholds and probabilities are calibrated on real contacts.
u.disc_p2: When the wanted direction is blocked by nearby obstacles, it also shows the most likely headings, that is the mountains that can scatter the signal.
u.disc_p3: The aim is to help you catch duct openings. It is not a guarantee: conditions change within minutes, and DX cluster and PSKReporter spots remain the real-time check.
u.disc_short: Semi-probabilistic calculation of tropospheric ducts from GFS profiles, following the theory of the scientific sources in the manual, with the most likely headings towards blocked directions. It helps you catch openings but does not guarantee them; real-time spots remain the check.
u.disc_hint: The callsign is used to log in to the clusters; an 8–10 character locator makes the terrain calculation more precise.
